title: Aug 26 Results + Aug 27 Preview: Eleven Wins and We're Just Getting Started
summary: Our model crushed it with 11-4 on Aug 26. Tomorrow's pick? Nationals again.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Momentum

Some days you just feel it clicking, you know? August 26th was one of those days where our model found its groove and didn't let go. We went 11-4 across the slate, hitting 73.3% of our picks. And honestly? The three misses tell just as good a story as the wins.

## The Story of August 26

Let's talk about what happened. The Diamondbacks took care of business against the Cubs just like we expected at 62% confidence. The Guardians, Pirates, and Phillies all delivered on the road—those are the kinds of wins that build your bankroll and your confidence.

But here's what I love: even our misses were close calls. The Tigers pick at 51%? The Nationals at 51%? Those were essentially coin flips, and that's exactly how we treated them. We're not pretending to have crystal balls here.

## The Human Element

You know what's wild? That Yankees pick at exactly 50% that somehow hit. Sometimes baseball is just baseball, and the most uncertain games break your way. Meanwhile, our highest-confidence pick—the Padres at 68%—sailed through without drama. That's the kind of variety that keeps this game interesting.

## Looking Ahead to August 27

And here's where things get interesting for tomorrow. We're going back to the well with the Nationals, who let us down yesterday in that nail-biter against the Rockies. Sometimes the best revenge is immediate.

Gabriel Hughes takes the mound for Colorado against Washington's Jake Irvin. Our model sees this as another tight one—50% confidence on the Nationals—but there's value in understanding the matchup dynamics here.

## Why We're Riding With Washington

Here's the thing about the Nationals right now—they're playing at home against a Rockies team that historically struggles away from Coors Field. Yes, it's a 50-50 call on paper, but sometimes the context matters as much as the numbers.

Jake Irvin has been steady for Washington, and while Gabriel Hughes has shown flashes for Colorado, the road environment is a different beast entirely for Rockies pitchers who are used to that thin Denver air.

Is this our highest conviction play ever? No. But after going 11-4 yesterday, we're trusting the process and staying disciplined. That's how you build long-term success in this game.

## The Bottom Line

August 26 reminded us why we do this. An 11-4 record isn't just luck—it's the model working, the analysis holding up, and the process proving itself. Tomorrow brings a fresh challenge with the Nationals, and we're ready for it.

Stay sharp, trust your research, and remember: in baseball, there's always another game tomorrow. And we'll be here breaking it all down.

*- Hana*
